77709-queer-people.title: Queer People
77709-queer-people.creator: Basil Thomson
77709-queer-people.description: A book by Basil Thomson. Real life is quite unlike detective fiction; in fact, in detective work fiction is stranger than truth. Sherlock Holmes, to whom I take off my hat with a silent prayer that he may never appear in the flesh, worked by induction, but not, so far as I am able to judge, by the only method which gets home, namely, organisation and hard work. He consumed vast quantities of drugs and tobacco.

arxiv-2102-02439.title: Towards Decentralized Human-Swarm Interaction by Means of Sequential Hand Gesture Recognition
arxiv-2102-02439.creator: Zahi Kakish, Sritanay Vedartham, Spring Berman
arxiv-2102-02439.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zahi Kakish, Sritanay Vedartham, Spring Berman. In this work, we present preliminary work on a novel method for Human-Swarm Interaction (HSI) that can be used to change the macroscopic behavior of a swarm of robots with decentralized sensing and control.

arxiv-2112-08492.creator: Josep Àlvarez Montaner 1, Manuel González Villa 2, Edwin León-Cardenal 3, Luis Núñez-Betancourt 4
arxiv-2112-08492.description: Abstract . We develop a theory of Bernstein-Sato polynomials for meromorphic functions. As a first application we study the poles of Archimedian local zeta functions for meromorphic germs. We also present a theory of multiplier ideals for meromorphic functions from the analytic and algebraic point of view.

arxiv-2210-01454.title: Event-Triggered Safe Stabilizing Boundary Control for the Stefan PDE System with Actuator Dynamics
arxiv-2210-01454.creator: Shumon Koga, Cenk Demir, Miroslav Krstic
arxiv-2210-01454.description: Abstract This paper proposes an event-triggered boundary control for the safe stabilization of the Stefan PDE system with actuator dynamics. The control law is designed by applying Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) to the continuous-time safe stabilizing controller developed in our previous work.

arxiv-2406-16206.title: Zero-Inflated Tweedie Boosted Trees with CatBoost for Insurance Loss Analytics
arxiv-2406-16206.creator: Banghee So, Emiliano A. Valdez
arxiv-2406-16206.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore advanced modifications to the Tweedie regression model in order to address its limitations in modeling aggregate claims for various types of insurance such as automobile, health, and liability. Traditional Tweedie models, while effective in capturing the probability and magnitude of claims, usually fall short in accurately representing the large incidence of zero claims.

arxiv-2412-17130.title: Derived Equivalences of Generalized Grassmannian Flops: D 4 D_{4} and G 2 † G_{2}^{\dagger} Cases
arxiv-2412-17130.creator: Ying Xie
arxiv-2412-17130.description: Abstract . We prove that the generalized Grassmannian flops of both D 4 D_{4} and G 2 † G_{2}^{\dagger} type induce derived equivalences, which provide new evidence for the DK conjecture by Bondal-Orlov and Kawamta. The proof is based on Kuznetsov’s mutation technique, which takes a sequence of mutations of exceptional objects. 1. Introduction 1.1.

arxiv-2502-14924.title: A Tale of Two Structures: Do LLMs Capture the Fractal Complexity of Language?
arxiv-2502-14924.creator: Ibrahim Alabdulmohsin, Andreas Steiner
arxiv-2502-14924.description: Abstract Language exhibits a fractal structure in its information-theoretic complexity (i.e. bits per token), with self-similarity across scales and long-range dependence (LRD). In this work, we investigate whether large language models (LLMs) can replicate such fractal characteristics and identify conditions—such as temperature setting and prompting method—under which they may fail.

arxiv-2509-08078.title: (A)Symmetric Complexity and the Quantum Mpemba Effect
arxiv-2509-08078.creator: Cameron Beetar, Jeff Murugan and Hendrik J.R. Van Zyl
arxiv-2509-08078.description: Abstract The Quantum Mpemba Effect (QME) — the counter-intuitive phenomenon where states further from equilibrium can relax faster than those closer to it — challenges standard expectations of quantum thermalization. In this work, we introduce Krylov complexity as a sensitive diagnostic for the QME.

arxiv-2509-17139.title: Optimal Parametrizations and Valuations
arxiv-2509-17139.creator: Reinhold Hübl, Craig Huneke, Sarasij Maitra, Vivek Mukundan
arxiv-2509-17139.description: Abstract . This article discusses a way for uniquely setting up the valuations for the minimal generators of the maximal ideal of a one dimensional complete reduced and irreducible local algebra over an algebraically closed field, when treated as a subring of its integral closure. Our observations are a generalization of the more well-studied case of a numerical semigroup ring.

pmc-12561867.description: Simple SummaryThe European grayling is an important salmonid species whose natural populations have declined due to anthropogenic pressure on riverine ecosystems. Production of sterile triploid females might offer a solution to this problem.

pmc-7616307.title: Death, social reform and the scrutiny of social welfare provision: the role of the contemporary inquest
pmc-7616307.creator: Edward Kirton-Darling
pmc-7616307.description: Suggesting there is an emerging and important focus on social welfare in inquests into death, this article argues that there is value for both social welfare and inquest scholarship in examination of links between the two. Emphasising the process of investigation, it aims to introduce the inquest to social welfare scholars, and proposes an agenda for research.
